title: fix(cli): os knowledge rebuild and status give the right answer behind a load balancer
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg3zXREECfPtgrM8TPQaxn1v)_

Fixes #37466

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：多节点部署的运维用命令行重建知识源时，进度查询打到别的节点不再直接报失败，而是改看所有节点一致的索引状态；查看状态时会说明应答节点上没有构建记录。
- 为什么做：知识库重建运维入口的后续修复，替多节点部署的运维和自动化脚本解决“构建在跑或已成功却被报失败”的问题。
- 出错会怎样：只影响命令行的结论，不影响服务端构建本身；可直接撤回本改动恢复旧行为。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

Design: the card's second option. The build record stays per node (no service change); the CLI falls back to the index state the store reports, which is the same on every node.

- `os knowledge rebuild` reads `index_status` once before it starts the build, as the baseline. A progress read answered by a node without this build's record (no record, or a record with another `startedAt`) is no longer an exit 1. It reads the index state instead: when the baseline was not `current` (never built, new fingerprint, changed recipe, no recipe hash), the index turning `current` means a complete build recorded itself (adapters record the recipe hash only in `completeBuild`), and the command exits 0, saying the counts were not read.
- When the baseline was already `current`, the index state cannot tell a running build from a finished one (a same-fingerprint rebuild opens no `building` generation in either adapter: `knowledge-memory` and `knowledge-pgvector` `beginBuild`), so the command keeps polling until a read reaches the building node, whose record decides.
- Failure is reported only on the build's own recorded failure (`failed` / `not-run`) or after the new `--timeout` (seconds, default 600, counted as polls times `--interval`) of reads that reach no record of this build and do not see the index turn `current`. The timeout message says the build may still be running and points at `os knowledge status`; a read that reaches the record starts the timeout again, so a single-node build is never cut off.
- `os knowledge status` labels the record as the answering node's, and when that node holds none says a build run on another node (or before a restart) is not shown, while the index state is the store's.
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` Knowledge section and a patch changeset.

Measured before designing: `index_status` already returns `index` (state, due, detail, held) from the store and `build` (or `null`) from the answering node, so "no record on this node" (`build: null`) and "never built" (`index.state: nothing`) are separate fields; no service change was needed.

## Tests

`packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/knowledge.test.ts`, new `describe` "a poll that lands on a node without the build record": still running (polls alternate between a node without the record and the building node, exit 0), succeeded (index turns `current`, exit 0), an older record on the answering node read as no record, an index already `current` waits for the building node and reports its recorded failure, `--timeout` exits 1 with its statement, and the timeout restarts on a read of the record. Existing rebuild tests gained the baseline read.

<details><summary>Readings at 91e9a5755</summary>

- `vitest run src/commands/knowledge/knowledge.test.ts`: Test Files 1 passed, Tests 12 passed (lock VERDICT command-exit 0).
- Ablation (rebuild.ts restored to the base c385d3bd1, tests kept): Tests 9 failed, 3 passed; restored, green.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: VERDICT command-exit 0 (incl. check:test-typecheck OK).

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The `index_status` answer carries no node identity, so `os knowledge status` can only say "the node that answered", never which node ran a build.
- A failed build seen only through other nodes leaves the index due; the CLI cannot read that failure from the store and ends on `--timeout`.

## Verification

Read first: `packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/rebuild.ts` (the fallback branch after the record check), then the new tests.
Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/commands/knowledge/knowledge.test.ts` shows 12 passed.
